pillar_reactions.evidence: He arrived pre-sold from three or four weeks of kettlebell finishers — 'I really like it. I like it more than doing the dumbbell weights and stuff. It's a lot of movement, mobility' — and named the specific mechanic that attracted him: 'what I really liked about you is that you want people to upload their videos and then you would give direct feedback on that.' He asked a long run of operational questions about session structure, frequency, duration, whether calisthenics is included and how the app works, and closed the section with 'This seems like it could be fun.' The mobility half was accepted without question.

Presented as sustainability-first, micronutrient-led, guidelines rather than gram weights, lower carb. The rep asked a genuinely good commitment question — 'are you willing to be clean six days a week in the guidelines, and then one day a week you can do whatever you want?' — and got a clean yes: 'I'm open to that.' He confirmed the philosophy fit at 'Okay, I'm okay with that. Yeah, all good.' Notable that a man who has never tracked anything, was a restaurateur his whole career and has sat at 19-20% body fat for life agreed to the pillar in three words and was not tested any further.

The rep read the prospect correctly and repositioned the pillar before presenting it: 'It's going to be less about accountability. It's more going to be about support and feedback.' That landed against a specific past grievance the prospect then volunteered: 'I've had people, trainers in the past, who would like message every few hours, what are you doing now? And it's just like, I'm working. Leave me alone.' He endorsed the fit — 'I like the fact that it's not overbearing as well' — but framed it as relief rather than value.

anchors.raw: Let me just see. Cause I think I'm on a subscription with my, the previous one. Uh, let me just figure out when that ends
anchors.note: The most actionable anchor on the call and the first thing he reached for after the price. He is mid-term on a competing app and treats the two as substitutes rather than complements. The rep never asked what it costs, when it ends, or proposed a start date that lines up with its expiry — a trivially solvable timing objection that was left as the reason to go away and think.

anchors.raw: so I would say probably 70% of our clients are business owners. We're very, very, very, very, very used to, um, framing invoices in certain ways for tax benefit
anchors.note: Rep-created and commercially very effective — the prospect responded 'Oh, that would be fantastic because I would like to write that off at the business expense' and it converted his 'I personally have no money' problem into a solved one. It is also the most serious compliance exposure in the batch and is flagged separately. Recorded here because as a sales mechanic it is now clearly a repeatable part of this rep's process, appearing on three calls in two days.

anchors.raw: I've had people, trainers in the past, who would like message every few hours
anchors.note: An established habit of paying for coaching, which supports price in principle. Never quantified — nobody asked what he paid or over what period, so the obvious comparison against $6,000 for six months was unavailable.

anchors.raw: I recently came out of a divorce about a year and a half ago and my ex-wife is constantly after me for more and more and more. So if I can put this in through my corporation, it'll be a much easier because I mean, I personally have no money, but my business is, you know, doing very well.
anchors.note: Recorded as supportive because the money genuinely exists at the corporate level and he engaged with $6,000 and $9,000 without resistance. The material point for the audit is the stated reason for routing it corporately, which involves an active matrimonial financial dispute, and which the rep neither questioned nor declined to assist with.

unmet_demand.want: Confirmation that abdominal definition is achievable, or honest information that it may not be, after multiple abdominal surgeries
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked it as plainly as it can be asked — 'I don't get abs, unfortunately. I don't even know if I can get abs, because I've had so many abdominal surgeries' — and received a generic answer about belly fat being the last to go and about getting to 10% being like making your first million. This is simultaneously a product question and a clinical one, and nothing in the offer produces an answer to either.

unmet_demand.want: A programme that works while travelling internationally every three or four months across the six-month term
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Raised explicitly as the reason he might not commit and never answered. The programme does have travel routines — this rep described them in detail on another call — and here the topic became a personal conversation about Mexico, Peru and Thailand instead.

unmet_demand.want: A resolution to his suspicion that he is overtraining — six days a week, high volume, no sweat, no progress
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised it twice, including 'I think I over-train right now' and 'I don't even break a sweat', and it was never diagnosed or answered. It is arguably the single most persuasive entry point into the sale and the programme's weekly adaptation is the direct answer, but the two were never connected.

unmet_demand.want: A safe loading progression designed around a recently reconstructed abdominal wall and a repaired hernia
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not only unmet but contradicted: the offer's headline guarantee is a 20 lb increase on every movement including swings and snatches, and no screening, clearance requirement or contraindication process exists at any point before payment.
